w3-meaning~idea.cta: What a prefix means on the Word road
w3-meaning~idea.title: What a prefix means
w3-meaning~idea.body: A prefix sits at the FRONT of a word and changes its meaning. "Un-" means not: unhappy is not happy. "Re-" means again: rebuild is build again.
w3-meaning~idea.more: I can say what a common prefix means.

w3-meaning~story.title: What a prefix means
w3-meaning~story.body: Quill has a box of little word-starts — un-, re-, pre-, mis- — and each one changes a word in its own way.

s3-pc~idea.cta: Phrase or clause? on the Sentence road
s3-pc~idea.title: Phrase or clause?
s3-pc~idea.body: A clause has a subject AND a verb: "the bell rang". A phrase is missing one of them: "after the bell". Look for someone doing something.
s3-pc~idea.more: I can tell whether a group of words is a phrase or a clause.

s3-pc~story.cta: Phrase or clause? on the Sentence road
s3-pc~story.title: Phrase or clause?
s3-pc~story.body: Some groups of words can stand up on their own two feet. Others need a sentence to lean on.
s3-pc~story.more: Taught at: Sentence 3 · Phrases and clauses — Phrase or clause?

s3-pc~eg.cta: Phrase or clause? on the Sentence road
s3-pc~eg.title: Phrase or clause?: for example

s3-pc~eg.more: Taught at: Sentence 3 · Phrases and clauses — Phrase or clause?

s3-main~idea.cta: The main clause on the Sentence road
s3-main~idea.title: The main clause
s3-main~idea.body: A main clause makes sense alone. A clause that begins with when, because, if or although cannot stand alone: it depends on the main clause.
s3-main~idea.more: I can find the main clause in a sentence.

s3-main~story.cta: The main clause on the Sentence road
s3-main~story.title: The main clause
s3-main~story.body: A long sentence often has a main clause — the part that could be a sentence all by itself — and a helper.
s3-main~story.more: Taught at: Sentence 3 · Phrases and clauses — The main clause.

s3-main~eg.cta: The main clause on the Sentence road
s3-main~eg.title: The main clause: for example
s3-main~eg.body: When the rain stopped, [the children ran outside].
s3-main~eg.more: Taught at: Sentence 3 · Phrases and clauses — The main clause.

wr3-imitate~idea.cta: In the same shape on the Writing road
wr3-imitate~idea.title: In the same shape
wr3-imitate~idea.body: Every sentence has a shape: it might start with “When…”, or list three things, or compare one thing to another. Keep the shape, change everything else. The app checks the shape — what you say is yours.
wr3-imitate~idea.more: I can write my own sentence in the shape of a great one.

wr3-imitate~story.cta: In the same shape on the Writing road
wr3-imitate~story.title: In the same shape
wr3-imitate~story.body: Writers learn from writers. Quill has found a beautiful sentence — now borrow its shape, and fill it with your own words.
wr3-imitate~story.more: Taught at: Writing 3 · Sentence imitation — In the same shape.

wr3-imitate~eg.cta: In the same shape on the Writing road

sp3-express~idea.cta: Say it like you mean it on the Stage
sp3-express~idea.title: Say it like you mean it
sp3-express~idea.body: Mark the poem: a pause at every comma and full stop, a longer pause at the end of each verse, and one word in each line to lean on. Speak some lines softer and some louder. The app measures your pauses and how far your volume moves — the feeling itself is for you and your grown-up to judge.
sp3-express~idea.more: I can recite a poem with expression: pauses, stress and changes of volume.

sp3-express~story.cta: Say it like you mean it on the Stage
sp3-express~story.title: Say it like you mean it
sp3-express~story.body: The same words can sound sleepy or thrilling. Expression is what you add.
sp3-express~story.more: Taught at: Speaking 3 · Recite with expression — Say it like you mean it.

li3-mood~idea.cta: How does it feel? on the Literature road
li3-mood~idea.title: How does it feel?
li3-mood~idea.body: The setting is where and when a story happens. The mood is the feeling the writing gives you: cosy, gloomy, spooky, joyful. Writers build mood from the setting and from their choice of words. "A gray cat walking a gray fence in a gray backyard": three grays make the moment feel dull and sad.
li3-mood~idea.more: I can say how a setting makes me feel.

li3-mood~story.cta: How does it feel? on the Literature road
li3-mood~story.title: How does it feel?
li3-mood~story.body: On a sunny morning Quill's wood is a playground. On a stormy night, the very same wood makes his fur stand on end. Same place, different feeling: that feeling is the mood.
li3-mood~story.more: Taught at: Literature 3 · Setting and mood — How does it feel?
